c.tagline: Nepal's serene lake city and gateway to the Annapurnas.

taxi.fareNote: Meters are rarely used; agree a fare before boarding, or use the Pathao and inDrive apps for fixed prices.

emergency.note: Fire: 101. Tourist Police assist around Lakeside; response times and resources can be limited.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The vibrant tourist heart of Pokhara stretching along Phewa Lake, lined with restaurants, bars with live music, trekking shops, cafes and boat jetties; the natural base for almost every visitor.

A quieter, greener lakeside stretch at the southern dam end of Phewa, with mountain views, calmer guesthouses and easy access to Devi's Fall; suits travelers wanting Lakeside proximity without the bustle.
A ridgetop village above the city famous for its Himalayan sunrise panorama over Machapuchare and the Annapurnas, and the launch point for paragliding; a scenic, tranquil stay for early risers.
Pokhara's historic core around the Bindhyabasini Temple, a traditional market street of old shops and shrines away from the tourist strip; best for a glimpse of local everyday life.
The busy commercial downtown around Mahendrapul and New Road, full of shops, banks and bus parks; practical and central for errands and transport rather than sightseeing.

water.note: Drink bottled, filtered or purified water only.

transit.pay: Cash is paid to the conductor on board; fares are cheap (roughly Rs 20-40). There is no smart-card or unified ticketing system.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am-7pm with little night service, so taxis and ride apps cover evenings.
transit.note: There is no metro or rail; visitors mostly walk around Lakeside, take taxis, or use the Pathao and inDrive apps. Rowboats cross Phewa Lake and local buses link the outlying wards and trailheads.

bus: Tourist coaches to Kathmandu and Chitwan

transit.m: Local bus / microbus toward the city center

tip.r: 10% is appreciated at tourist restaurants without a service charge; rounding up for guides, porters and drivers is common but not obligatory.

landmarks: Phewa Lake
Rowboats drift past forested shores as Machhapuchhare's fishtail summit reflects in Nepal's second-largest lake, the serene heart of Pokhara.
World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa)
This gleaming white Buddhist stupa crowns a ridge above Phewa Lake, delivering sunrise panoramas across the city to the entire Annapurna range.
Sarangkot
Pokhara's classic dawn viewpoint watches the Himalaya blush pink, then fills with paragliders launching out over the valley by mid-morning.
Tal Barahi Temple
A two-tiered pagoda dedicated to the goddess Durga occupies a tiny island in Phewa Lake, reached by brightly painted wooden rowboats.
International Mountain Museum
Exhibits on Everest pioneers, Sherpa culture and mountain ecology honor the world's 8,000-meter peaks, with a climbable model peak outside.
Davis Falls (Devi's Fall)
This curious waterfall vanishes into an underground gorge, taking its name from a Swiss visitor swept away by its waters in 1961.
Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave
Across the road from Davis Falls, a sacred Shiva shrine descends into a dripping cavern where the vanished waterfall dramatically reappears underground.
Bindhyabasini Temple
Pokhara's oldest temple, set on a hillock in the Old Bazaar, hums with bells, devotees and clear-morning views of Annapurna and Machhapuchhare.
Begnas Lake
Quieter than Phewa, this emerald lake east of town rewards visitors with rustic fishing villages, swimming coves and perfect mountain reflections.
Mahendra and Bat Caves
Twin limestone caverns on Pokhara's northern edge offer shrines, stalactites and a squeeze-through exit crawl past thousands of roosting bats.

train.note: Pokhara has no railway and no line has ever been built into the hill country. Nepal's only passenger rail is the 69 km broad-gauge Jaynagar - Janakpur - Bijalpura service run by the Nepal Railway Company in the eastern Terai, roughly 500 km away, which crosses into India at Jaynagar and is the country's sole cross-border train. From Pokhara, reaching it means a full day by bus, so in practice every journey here is by road or by air.

bus.note: No scheduled coach crosses the border from Pokhara; you take a Nepali bus to Sunauli / Belahiya (8-9 hours) or Kakarbhitta and change to Indian services on the far side, and tickets sold in Lakeside as 'direct to Varanasi or Delhi' always involve that change. Tourist coaches to Kathmandu (6-7 hours, Rs700-1200) and Chitwan leave early in the morning from the Tourist Bus Park near Mustang Chowk, and Greenline runs a daily air-conditioned service between Thamel and Lakeside with lunch included for around US$20. Cheaper local and night buses use the Prithvi Chowk bus park, and the Baglung bus park serves the trekking trailheads at Nayapul, Beni and Jomsom. Book tourist coaches through a Lakeside agent or your guesthouse the day before.

ferry.note: Nepal is landlocked and has no ferry network. The wooden doonga rowing boats and small motor launches on Phewa Lake that cross to the Tal Barahi temple island and the foot of the World Peace Pagoda are recreational hire rather than scheduled transport, paid for by the hour at the Lakeside jetties.

half.name: Australian Camp
half.blurb: Foothill village reached by a short drive and hike offers open views of the Annapurna and Machapuchare ranges without a multi-day trek.

half.name: Ghandruk
half.blurb: Gurung village in the Annapurna foothills, reached by a few hours of driving and walking, has stone-paved lanes and mountain views.

full.name: Lumbini
full.blurb: Buddha's birthplace, about four hours south, holds the Maya Devi Temple and monasteries built by dozens of Buddhist nations.
